### R30 — the US index and the ETF flows as MARKET-direction and sizing information: what the Nasdaq 100's recent move, crypto's lag behind it, and yesterday's ETF flow say about the equal-weight basket's next 1h, 4h and 1d, and what the index's session and volatility say about the SIZE of that move (registered 2026-10-08 on Vadim's "1", before the code was written and before any basket bar was read against the index or the flows; read 2026-10-08: DIRECTION 0 of 27 clear — the index's last hour carries into the basket's next 1–4 h in every year (ix_1h +0.025 / +0.028, family-wise p 0.005) but under the round trip's bar, CLOSED at 1h and NOT DETECTABLE at 4h; the flows nothing (MDE 0.04–0.37); SIZING ix_open CLEARS at 4h (partial +0.059 on volratio_4h, t 8), a described sizing row for a future rule; nothing licensed for a trade)
Question:      R26 and R27 asked the index and the flows PER NAME (which name beats its peers) and found nothing. §9 #7's
               other reading is the market itself: one number a day or an hour for the whole market against one series.
               Does what the Nasdaq 100 just did, or how far crypto has lagged behind it, say which way the WHOLE market
               goes over the next hour, four hours or day (direction)? And does the index's session (open / closed) or its
               own volatility say how BIG the basket's next move is, beyond what crypto's own recent volatility already
               says (sizing)? A ceiling audit in R6's frame (Principle 2): no model, no book, no confirmation fold, no
               download — the index is `data/index_1m.parquet` (DATA.md `index_1m`), the flows `data/etf_flows.parquet`
               (`etf_flows`), both on the work VM since R26 / R27.
Frame:         R6's, exactly (`ft2/market.py`): the equal-weight basket of the pairs present (≥ 5) on the 5-minute grid;
               the label at h = the basket's forward log move over h divided by its trailing 1-week σ·√h, clipped at ±5
               (R6's; a standardised label, not money — the money is the described view below, in actual returns); the
               statistic = the whole-sample uncentred correlation Σf·y/√(Σf²Σy²) with the HAC t of the daily sums
               (`market.ic_stats`), per calendar year beside; the null = 200 circular shifts of the label series by a
               whole number of days, 60 ≤ k ≤ days − 60, the SAME draws (seed 0) for every number; signed features enter
               clipped at ±5, level features as their rank − ½ (`market.encode`); horizons 1h, 4h, 1d. The |move| target
               for sizing = R6's "vol" bet: the rank of |label|, against the rank of the feature.
               Family-wise p: per family, per draw the largest |t| over ALL its rows (features × the three horizons) — one
               bar for the family, stricter than R6's per-horizon one.
Index rules:   R26's, unchanged: US100 (the Nasdaq 100 CFD); a minute stamped ts is known from ts + 1 min; the value at an
               instant s is the close of the last known minute; OPEN at s if that minute is within 15 min of s, CLOSED
               otherwise (weekends, the daily break 21:00–22:59 UTC, holidays, and a missing hour — 2023-02 → 07 is thin);
               nothing interpolated. m_h = the index's log move from its value at t − h to its value at t, bps; σ_ix = the
               sd of its 1-hour moves over its last 30 days of hours open at both ends (≥ 200 such hours, else NaN).
Family A —     the INDEX, on R6's bars (FP+F0+F1+F2, 2020-05-03 → 2024-08-31, 1,578 days, 454,464 bars). Eight features,
               fixed here, each known strictly before t:
               direction (signed, in units of σ_ix·√h so the ±5 clip is R6's):
                 ix_1h     m_1h / (σ_ix·√1), read when the index is OPEN at t and at t − 1 h, else NaN
                 ix_4h     m_4h / (σ_ix·√4), OPEN at t and at t − 4 h
                 ix_24h    m_24h / (σ_ix·√24), OPEN at t (the start whatever its age: on Monday morning, Friday's close)
                 ix_gap    read only when CLOSED at t: the index's move over its last 240 traded minutes before the close in
                           force / (σ_ix·√4) — what it did going into the break; open hours NaN
                 lag_4h    how far crypto has LAGGED the index over the last 4 h: b·ix_4h − mret_4h, where mret_4h is R6's
                           (the basket's 4h move in its own σ units) and b = the least-squares slope of the basket's 24-hour
                           σ-unit move (R6's mret_1d) on the index's 24-hour σ-unit move (ix_24h's number), at hourly steps
                           over the last 30 days of hours with the index open (≥ 200 such hours, else NaN); positive = the
                           basket is behind the index. Read where ix_4h is read.
                           AMENDED 2026-10-08, before the code read any real bar (commit after 1168642): as first written, b
                           was the slope of the basket's 1-HOUR move on the index's 1-hour move. The registered test on
                           made-up bars (a basket that follows the index over several hours) read lag_4h with the WRONG sign
                           under that b — a contemporaneous hourly slope sees only the part of the response that arrives
                           within the hour, so a basket still catching up on older moves looks "ahead". The 24-hour slope
                           is the response the basket eventually makes; under it the planted follower reads positive and an
                           instantaneous follower reads zero. The family, the gate and the expectation are unchanged.
                 lag_24h   the same at 24 h: b·ix_24h − mret_1d. Read where ix_24h is read.
               sizing (levels, read only against the |move| target):
                 ix_open   1 if the index is OPEN at t, else 0
                 ix_vol    the sd of the index's 1-hour moves over its last 24 traded hours (≥ 12) over σ_ix, a ratio like
                           R6's volratio; read when OPEN at t
               Family A-direction = 6 × 3 horizons = 18 numbers; family A-sizing = 2 × 3 = 6 numbers (its own family).
               The sizing PARTIAL, per number: the same IC with the |move| rank replaced by its residual on the rank of
               R6's volratio_4h (one coefficient fitted over the scored bars) — what the index adds to what the basket's
               own recent volatility already says. Reported with its HAC t.
Family B —     the FLOWS, on F2 alone (2024-01-03 → 2024-08-31, 242 days; F1 holds no flow; R27's F(t), F5(t), the
               known-at d + 1 09:00 UTC, the 300 US$m cut — unchanged). Three signed features, scaled so the clip is ±5
               at five sd: flow = F(t)/300; flow_5d = F5(t)/(300·√5); flow_big = F(t)/300 where |F(t)| ≥ 300, else NaN.
               Family B = 3 × 3 = 9 numbers. The shift null on 242 days: 60 ≤ k ≤ 182, 200 draws. ETH's flows not read.
Validity:      read first or the run is void. (1) The frame is R6's: R6's 17 features computed in the same run on the same
               bars with the same 200 shifts reproduce `output/market/screen.parquet` (the VM's, written 2026-09-21) —
               the directional and vol IC, t and per-year IC of every feature × horizon to 1e-6, and every draw's t at 4h
               to 1e-6. (2) No index minute is used before it is known and no flow before d + 1 09:00 UTC (asserted in the

Gate:          validity PASS, then per number of A-direction and B:

Commands:      on the work VM, in this order —
                 `vm.sh bg r30a ceiling --target basket --family index`              → output/market_index.md, output/market_index/
                 `vm.sh bg r30b ceiling --target basket --family etf --folds F2`     → output/market_etf.md,   output/market_etf/

(registered 2026-10-09 on Vadim's "let's go with F5" (P8 decision F5), before the rule was written and before it saw any real bar; stage 1 read 2026-10-09: PASSED by the gate as written — maker net +2.05 bps a trade [−6.24, +10.34], shuffle p 0.010, flip p 0.010, no calendar year under −5 — the gross is real (R30's continuation, +6.45 maker / +9.43 taker) and the money is about zero; the measured se (4.2 on 1,578 days) makes F3+F4 unable to confirm an effect of this size (se ≈ 7.6, MDE ≈ 21): stage 2 = P8 decision G, DECIDED 2026-10-09 by Vadim: "G1" — NOT RUN, R31 PARKED, F3+F4 unspent for the market factor; stage 2 read — (never))
Question:      R30 certified that the Nasdaq 100's move over its last hour carries into the equal-weight basket's next one to
               four hours — IC +0.025 at 1h and +0.028 at 4h, positive in each of 2020 → 2024, family-wise p 0.005, the same
               on US500 — and found it under the bar a round trip on the basket needs (0.061 at 1h, 0.034 at 4h). Decision F5
               asks whether a MAKER execution pays it. Two corrections of F5's premise, written before any number: (1) at
               4h the bar R30 missed IS the maker bar — R6's #7 is the smaller of "maker, all bars" (0.034; a maker round
               trip on the basket 7.15 bps against a mean |4h move| of 95.7) and "taker, most volatile tenth" (also 0.034),
               so a maker price on every bar cannot clear what R30 read; what can is trading only the hours whose index move
               is large, where the move per trade grows against a round trip that does not. (2) The harness's maker is
               path-dependent (`backtest.price`): a continuation rule buys what just rose, and its resting order is filled
               when the basket comes back — the adverse selection is the rule's own and sits inside gross (R8 lost 5.5 bps
               of gross to it). So the question is: the index's last hour, read once an hour with the serving lag, traded
               at its sign on the whole basket only when the hour's move is at least one of the index's own hourly sigmas,
               held four hours, as a maker — does it make money after costs through the harness, and is a confirmation
               read on F3+F4, the only cells no market-wide question has read, worth spending?
Rule:          `ft2/rules.py::IndexHour`, name `ixhour4h`, fixed here, nothing fitted, nothing searched. On the 5-minute grid,
               at every bar t = H + L where H is an hour's close (H:00 UTC) and L = 3 bars (15 min, the serving lag: the
               index's close at H is known 10 min after the hour from a feed like Yahoo's ES=F, and the decision is taken at
               the next 5m bar; the harness then executes 1 bar later, LATENCY, so the fill is at H + 20 min):
                 f(H)  = ix_1h at H exactly as R30 computed it (`market_ext`: the index's log move from H − 1 h to H in bps over
                         σ_ix(H), the sd of its 1-hour moves over its last 30 days of hours open at both ends, ≥ 200 such hours
                         else NaN; read only when the index is OPEN at H and at H − 1 h under R26's rule — the minute in force
                         is known from its stamp + 1 min and OPEN means within 15 min of H; closed hours, the daily break, the
                         weekend and the thin months give NaN and no trade). The value used at t is the value at H: nothing
                         after H enters (asserted by a test and by the harness's causal check).
                 trade   |f(H)| ≥ θ = 1 → side = sign(f(H)), EVERY pair present at t, one unit each, held 48 bars (4 h); one
                         position per pair (the harness's book rule), so a basket opened at H stands until H + 4 h + L + 1 bars
                         and the hours inside it are skipped as `position_open` — about one basket entry per four to five open
                         hours at most. θ = 1 is R30's money-view cut ("after the index rose / fell ≥ 1σ_ix"), the one cut
                         written before R30 was read; it is not chosen from R30's rows (R30's screen was linear on all bars).
                 side    both sides, symmetric (R30's IC is one number; the basket's drift, +4.8 bps a 4h bar on seen data, helps
                         the longs and costs the shorts — `hedged` is zero by construction on a basket rule, so the drift is
                         read from the long-and-short-apart table, not gated).

(registered 2026-10-12 on Vadim's "let's go as recommended" (P8 decision H: H1 + H2), before the rule was written and before it saw any real bar; stage 1 read 2026-10-12: GATE FAILED on its per-year condition — taker net +10.67 bps a trade [−10.97, +32.30], both nulls p ≤ 0.025, but 2020 −7.1, 2022 −14.5 and 2024 −21.4 against a bar of −5; every bit of the money is the long side (+35.5 [+4.9, +66.1]), the short side −15.8; PARKED, no variant, decision I not opened, F3+F4 never read)
Question:      R6's screen (2026-09-21, `output/market.md`) carries a one-day row that was reported and never gated or acted on:
               the basket's trailing 30-day return (`mret_30d`) against the basket's NEXT DAY — IC +0.0705 (t 2.9), positive in
               each of 2020 → 2024 (+0.021, +0.136, +0.032, +0.081, +0.056), family-wise p 0.0498 among seventeen features, against
               a 1d bar of 0.0131 (maker, all bars) / 0.0188 (taker). R6's gate was written for 4h only; at 4h the same feature
               read +0.030 with p_fw 0.075 and was not recorded, and R8 traded the 4h BOUNCE conditional on the trend, not the
               trend. The row met the letter of R6's gate paragraph ("a single feature with family-wise p ≤ 0.05 AND one sign in
               all five years is recorded as a hypothesis for a new registration") at a horizon the gate did not look at — a miss
               of the record, written down here as what it is: a hypothesis on seen bars. The question: the basket's 30-day sign,
               read once a day and traded on every pair for a day, one unit each — does it make money after costs through the
               harness, in actual returns, with funding charged on the position's value, and what can that evidence license?
Rule:          `ft2/rules.py::Trend1d`, name `trend1d`, fixed here, nothing fitted, nothing searched. On the 5-minute grid, at
               the one decision bar a day t whose stamp is 00:00 UTC (the bar that closes at midnight):
                 blr(t)  = R6's basket: the equal-weight mean over the pairs with a bar of their 5m log returns (≥ MIN_PAIRS = 5
                           pairs, else NaN), cumulated — `ceiling.basket` on `log(close).diff()`, the same line `market.derive`
                           and `trendfall4h` (R8) use; nothing after t enters (the harness's causal check, and a test).
                 s(t)    = sign(blr(t) − blr(t − 8,640 bars)): the 30-day return's sign, R6's `mret_30d` without its
                           volatility scaling (a positive scale; the sign is the same). s = 0 or NaN → no trade.
                 trade     side = s on EVERY pair with a close at t, one unit each, held 288 bars (one day); executed one bar later
                           (LATENCY: the 00:05 close), so the position stands 00:05 → 00:05 and the next day's 00:00 decision is
                           accepted by the book rule (one position per pair; p = p_prev + hold is not blocked): a round trip is
                           paid EVERY day, which is the conservative count — a position held until the sign flips is a described
                           row below, read from the saved fills, not a rule the harness runs.
                 why 00:00 the UTC day's boundary, the one the harness's day-clustered interval and R6's per-day statistics
                           use; a funding settlement instant, so a position opened after it pays the 08:00, the 16:00 and the next
                           00:00 — three settlements a day, as any one-day hold on these contracts. No hour was looked at or
                           searched; R6's screen read every bar of the day, this rule reads one.
               Three numbers: trend_days = 30 (R6's longest window, the one the screen reported), hour = 0, hold = 288. Both sides
               symmetric (R6's IC is one number). The pre-history is in the rule's reach: the archive's klines start
               2019-12-31, FP's first scored bar is 2020-05-03, and five pairs have bars from 2020-01-31, so blr and its 30-day lag
               exist from FP's first day.
Contrast:      mean net bps per unit of notional vs zero and vs both nulls (the day-shuffled price path, 200 draws; the flip
               null: every day's sides × one random sign); PRIMARY execution `taker` — path-independent, R8's and R9's primary;

Described:     decides nothing; licenses nothing on any fold. (a) The HELD position, from the saved taker and maker fills: the daily

### R33 — the demeaned ±1 % book imbalance as a ceiling screen on the twelve: does the within-pair, within-month variation of the book carry any of P2's one-day IC, or was it all the slow level R9 and R11 could not trade? (registered 2026-10-12 on Vadim's "let's go as recommended" (P8 decision H: H1 + H2), before the code was written and before any book row was read demeaned; read 2026-10-12: CLEARS by the gate as written — the demeaned imbalance at 1d IC −0.0224 (t −3.28, se 0.0068), p_family 0.005 on BOTH nulls, F1 −0.025 / F2 −0.020, above the maker bar 0.0106 and the taker bar 0.0182; validity PASS to 0.0; the fast part is 80–100 % of the imbalance's variance and carries more than half of P2's IC — R9's reading was wrong; a hypothesis on seen cells; the breadth step is P8 decision J, Vadim's)
Question:      P2's screen found one per-pair directional signal at one day: the ±1 % book imbalance, IC −0.039 (t −4.3,
               family-wise p 0.005, 88 % of months the same sign; relative −0.032, p_fw 0.015) — "the most interesting cell".
               Two rules on the raw imbalance lost (R9 both sides, R11 long only), and R9's reading was that the pooled IC is
               carried by the LEVEL of a pair's imbalance over weeks (a persistently bid-heavy book while the pair drifts down),
               which a daily trade at 12 bps a round trip cannot collect; §7 (b) left one question open since 2026-09-22: the
               imbalance DEMEANED by the pair's own trailing month — does the part of the imbalance that changes from day to day
               predict the pair's next day at all? R15 says book features add nothing to the RELATIVE bet held out among the
               twelve; this is the directional own-pair bet, and it has never been read demeaned. A ceiling screen, not a rule:
               it spends no fold and licenses, at most, a breadth step.
Audit:         `ft2/book_ext.py` (its docstring is the specification), `ft2 ceiling --target pairs --family depth`. P2's frame
               exactly (`ceiling.panel` on the twelve, `derive`, F1+F2 embargoed as the scored sample, `ic_screen`'s three
               statistics: the directional pooled IC on per-pair ranks, the relative cross-sectional Spearman, the vol IC), on
               three bar × pair features built from ONE source, `ceiling.depth_frames`' imb1 — the ±1 % imbalance from the archive
               book's last ~30 s sample strictly before t, the definition the screen and the rules share:
                 depth_imb_1        the raw imbalance, P2's feature — the VALIDITY row (below), not a question;
                 depth_imb_1_lvl30  its trailing-month mean: the mean over the 8,640 bars ending at t (≥ 4,320 of them present), the
                                    SLOW part — described, not gated (a feature this slow is flattered by a day-shuffle null; R6);
                 depth_imb_1_dm     = depth_imb_1 − depth_imb_1_lvl30, the FAST part — THE registered feature. raw = lvl30 + dm
                                    exactly wherever both exist (asserted). The month (30 days) is §7 (b)'s "trailing month",

### R35 — the slow book at a longer hold: does the month's mean of the ±1 % imbalance, found twice, pay a round trip held 3 or 7 days, in money, on the 43 names? (registered 2026-10-12 on Vadim's "go with K1" (P8 decision K), before the code was written and before any label beyond one day was computed on a book feature; read 2026-10-12: 0 of 4 clear, every row NOT DETECTABLE — the slow level at 7 days m_c −55.7 bps a leg but se 35.6 (u −1.56, MDE 100); at 3 days −27.8, u −1.99, p_family 0.11; the raw at 3 days −16.1, u −2.34, p_family 0.051 — two rows at the bar's edge, none over it; validity PASS; PARKED as "real at one day, not shown to pay at a week on 43 names"; the sample's MDE at 7 days is seven times the cost)
Question:      The ±1 % book imbalance's one-day lean is a property of these perpetuals' books: found on eleven names (P2, −0.039;
               R33) and again on 32 names their screen never saw (R34, −0.036), and on BOTH universes its SLOW part — the trailing
               month's mean of the imbalance, `depth_imb_1_lvl30` — reads −0.055 at one day (R33 t −2.3, R34 t −2.8). Two daily rules
               on the raw imbalance lost (R9, R11): a 12-bps round trip every day against a signal that moves over weeks. A round trip
               costs the same whether a position is held a day or a week (R22's premise). Held 3 or 7 days, do the names whose month's
               book is most ask-heavy earn more than those whose month's book is most bid-heavy — in the MEAN, in bps per leg, in
               actual returns with funding inside, by more than the round trip? A ceiling audit in R22's frame: no model, no book, no
               fold spent, no download (the 43 names' book and candles for F1+F2 are in hand).
Cells:         the 43 names whose book is in hand — the eleven of the twelve with bars before the end of F2 and `universe.NEW`'s 32 —
               on HOURLY decision bars (R22's grid: 24 a day; the feature moves over weeks and the null shifts by whole days) of F1+F2,
               embargoed, every source cut at 2024-09-01. A cell is read at a hold if its label exists (the last 3 or 7 days of F2 have
               none). The eleven and the 32 enter as ONE set of cells (a tenth of 43 is 4 names a side); the two universes apart are
               described rows, not the statistic.
Holds:         two, fixed here: 864 bars (3 days) and 2,016 bars (7 days). One day (288) is the reference row (read at the IC level by
               R33 and R34; it can clear nothing here).
Label:         `horizon.labels`, unchanged: what a long position earns before trading costs — exit / entry − 1 from the close one bar
               after t to the close `hold` bars later, in actual returns, MINUS the funding a long pays over those bars, each payment on
               the position's value (`backtest.load_costs`' `fundval`; the 32's funding is in `funding_archive`), bps. Against the
               peers: minus the mean over the bar's cells with a label (R22).
Signals:       the FAMILY, two, each from `book_ext.features_depth` (one definition with R33/R34, sampled at the hourly bars), known
               strictly before t: `depth_imb_1_lvl30` (PRIMARY — the slow level, the mean over the 8,640 bars ending at t with ≥ 4,320
               present) and `depth_imb_1` (the raw imbalance, found twice at one day). Registered sign: NEGATIVE — a bid-heavy month
               (high signal) precedes the worse week, so the top-minus-bottom leg M should be negative. Described, outside the
               family: `depth_imb_1_dm` (the within-month part, which did not travel in R34).
Statistic:     R22's M, by `horizon._tenths`: per bar with ≥ MIN_CELLS cells that have the signal and the label, k = the tenth of them,
               rounded (4 of 43); the mean label-against-peers of the k highest by the signal minus that of the k lowest, HALVED — bps
               per leg of a top-against-bottom book, before trading costs, funding inside; averaged per day; M = the mean over days.
               Two-sided: a signal that sorts the wrong way round is a signal, recorded as "with the opposite sign".
Null:          R22's: the labels move by a whole number of days, the same for every name and bar (a circular shift of the scored days,
               time of day kept, whole rows move), EVERY admissible shift, none drawn — admissible if no day receives the labels of a
               day nearer than gap = 30 (the feature's window) + 7 (the longest hold) + 1 = 38 days in either direction, the same shifts
               for both holds: 485 − 2 × 38 + 1 = 410 shifts. Why not day shuffles: at these holds neighbouring days' labels share
               2/3 or 6/7 of their window, which a shift keeps and a shuffle breaks (R22). A name keeps its own labels, so a lasting
               link between a name's level and its drift survives in the null and earns no credit — the right null for a LEVEL signal.
               Per signal × hold: centre = the mean of M over the shifts, se = their sd; M_c = M − centre, u = M_c / se; the family
               2 × 2 = 4: per shift the largest |u| of the four → the family-wise p of a real |u|. The HAC se over days (lags = days of
               the hold + 1) reported beside, deciding nothing.
Cost:          15 bps per leg, FIXED here before any number: 10.0 of fees (VIP 0 taker, both legs) + the 43's spread and impact at
               10,000 USDT — 2.3 a round trip on the eleven from the tape (P1), about 5.2 on the 32 from the candle proxy (DATA.md:
               taker_leg_other p50 2.6 a leg), weighted by names 4.4 → 14.4, rounded UP to 15. The cells' actual mean taker round
               trip on the extreme tenths (`ceiling.bar_cost`, the proxy for the 32) is REPORTED beside it; funding is inside the label.
               A maker price is not assumed (the 32 have no maker measurement).

### R37 — the forced-flow signature: does an hour in which open interest left while the price moved far and the takers pushed with it predict a reversal over the next 1 and 4 hours, per name, on the screener members and on the twelve? (registered 2026-10-12 on Vadim's "M1" (P8 decision M), before the code was written and before any metrics row was read against a 1h or 4h label; read 2026-10-13: 0 of 8 clear — seven rows "CLEARS AS THE PLAIN REVERSAL" and one CLOSED: the footprint-weighted reversal is real (u 3–5) but SMALLER than the plain hourly reversal on the same cells (u_Δ −3 … −7); the forced hours (4,932 on the members, 0.7 % of cells) fade for +1.7 bps at 1h and −1.0 at 4h against a round trip of 18; validity PASS; PARKED as "not shown on these cells at 1–4h: the footprint subtracts from the reversal it was to sharpen"; what stands is the plain cross-sectional 1–4h reversal, IC +0.02 … +0.03 (u 7–11), far under its cost bar)
Question:      Every per-name signal read so far was a level or a slow mean (funding, premium, open interest over volume, the book's
               month) at one day or longer. This is a different kind of thing: an EVENT. When a leveraged position is liquidated the
               exchange closes it at market — open interest falls, the price moves in the direction of the forced trades, and the taker
               flow is one-sided in that direction, all within the hour; the move is not information, it is forced, and the standard
               expectation is that part of it comes back over the next hours. The archive has no liquidation file; its 5-minute
               `metrics` (open interest in contracts, the taker buy/sell volume ratio) on the 199 members and the twelve are the
               footprint. P2 read the open-interest change ALONE at 1h on the twelve (0.011, a fifth of the bar) and the plain 1h
               reversal is a known, sub-cost fact (P2: the relative 1h bet on the last 15 minutes' return, IC 0.030, "very real, far too
               small"). The question is the INTERACTION: does the reversal after an hour that carries the footprint beat the plain
               reversal, by enough to be read, on the names a screener picks from and on the twelve?
Cells:         R26's frame. OUTSIDE: R18's cells exactly (`audit.frame` on `output/backtest/r18_transferbook_1d`: hourly decision bars of
               F1+F2, embargoed, the block's 60 members, the twelve left out; 694,501 cells, 188 names — the membership mask; the labels
               here are at 12 and 48 bars, so a cell is read where that label exists). THE TWELVE: `audit_index.cells_twelve` on the same
               hourly grid (checked against R14's run as R26 did). The same grid, the same shifts for both universes.
Labels:        z_h = the log move from the close one bar after t to the close h bars later over σ_1w·√h, clipped at ±5 (`horizon.run`'s
               `Zh`, the frame R20–R27 used), at h = 12 (1h) and 48 (4h); the money view below in ACTUAL returns.
Ingredients:   three numbers per name and hourly bar t, each known strictly before t (a metrics row stamped ts is used from ts + 5 min and
               carried at most 3 bars, R20's rule; the candles are closed at t):
                 move_1h   = the name's log return over the last 12 bars over σ_1w·√12 — the hour's move in its own sigmas;
                 oi_chg_1h = log OI(t) − log OI(t − 12 bars), OI the archive's `sum_open_interest` (contracts) — negative: positions left;
                 taker_1h  = the mean over the last 12 rows of log(taker buy volume / taker sell volume) — positive: buyers took.
Family:        two signed features, the reversal direction built in so that a POSITIVE IC is the hypothesis, × two horizons × two
               universes = 8 numbers:
                 rev_oi   = −move_1h × max(−oi_chg_1h, 0)     — the hour's move reversed, weighted by how much open interest LEFT (zero
                                                                 when it grew: a move on new positions is not a liquidation);
                 rev_flow = rev_oi × |taker_1h| × 1[sign(taker_1h) = sign(move_1h)]   — the same, only when the takers pushed WITH the
                                                                 move (forced sellers in a fall, forced buyers in a rise), weighted by
                                                                 how one-sided they were; zero otherwise.
               Nothing is fitted; no threshold enters the family (the statistic ranks across names, so the features' scale is immaterial).
Reference:     described, no verdict, the same frame: rev_1h = −move_1h (the plain reversal — the known fact the family must beat);
               oi_chg_1h alone; taker_1h alone; −move_1h × |oi_chg_1h| (the OI change in EITHER direction — if this reads as rev_oi,
               the "left" matters nothing); and R18's forecast. For each family number the PAIRED difference against rev_1h on the same

### R39 — the maker cost at the trade level on the twelve: a resting order at the touch, its queue position from the ladder, filled by the trades that follow — is the maker round trip the 7 bps every maker verdict in §8 stands on, or 4, or 10? (registered 2026-10-13 on Vadim's "P1" (P8 decision P), before any trade file of the window was fetched and before the code was written; read 2026-10-13: VALIDITY PASS — the twelve's median effective maker round trip 8.43 bps (the missed move excluded; 12.9 with it) against 6.70 for the harness's bar-level maker on the same placements and 6.90 for P1's minute-level day numbers: the maker path is NARROWER than the record said by about 1.7 bps a round trip — OPEN on seven names, NARROWER on five (ETH, XRP, ZEC, PEPE, HYPE, by 1.5 … 2.3), CLOSED on none; fills come by sweep (90–99 % of fills), not by the queue, and arrive in seconds; the harness over-fills by 2–4 points and understates the drift after the fill by about 0.5 bps)
Question:      P1 measured the maker's cost at the MINUTE level (`cost.maker`): an order resting at the minute's last traded bid (a buy) or ask
               (a sell), "filled" if a later minute's low (high) trades strictly through that price within 5 / 15 / 30 minutes, the adverse
               drift the close H minutes on against the resting price, conditional on the fill. It gave fill shares of 86–97 % within 15
               minutes, adverse drifts of −1.0 … −2.9 bps, maker round trips of 6.0 … 9.6 bps (`maker_rt_15 = 2 × 2.0 − 2 × maker_adv_15`),
               and wrote its own caveat: "coarse (1-minute, queue position unknown); trade-level check on a short raw window is parked
               (§7)" with the trigger "a verdict hinges on the 4-bps taker-vs-maker difference". The harness's `maker` (P3) rests at the
               execution bar's CLOSE, fills if a later bar's low (high) trades strictly through within 3 bars, else crosses at the close 3
               bars on; it reproduced P1's day average (−7.2 against −7.4) and cannot know which orders fill either. Three verdicts now
               hinge on that number: R31 (+2 bps net as a maker), R38 (+20 on 416 trades), and the 4h cross-sectional reversal (R37: IC
               0.023 against a maker bar of 0.027 and a maker-with-timing bar of 0.015). The question is the one P1 parked: at the TRADE
               level, with the order's place in the queue known, what share of resting orders fill within 15 minutes, how long they wait,
               what the price does to them, and what the maker round trip really is — per name and hour — and does the harness's
               bar-level maker over- or under-state it? Not a signal: no rule is evaluated, no label is read.
Window:        2026-08-15 00:00 → 2026-08-28 23:59 UTC, 14 whole days — the only weeks for which the collector's full ladder (`orderbook_
               levels`, ~12 s, 100 levels with quantities) exists for all twelve (from 2026-08-14 03:12 on ADA, AVAX, LINK, XRP; from 08-05
               on the eight others) with the archive's trades beside it. The window sits in F5, which is frozen for R17's read: this read
               evaluates no rule and no label on it — prices, trades and the book only, as P1 read the tape over 2023 → 2026-09 — and
               the block says so.
Data:          (1) the archive's daily `aggTrades` for the twelve over the window — `ft2 archive aggTrades --symbols <the twelve> --start
               2026-08-15 --end 2026-08-28` (daily files, sha256-checked, resumable; `data/raw/external/binance/aggTrades/<SYM>/`; ≈ 12 × 14
               × 15–45 MB ≈ 4–6 GB zipped; the VM has 89 GB free after R36). `ft2 tape --keep-zip` is NOT used: it skips a day whose
               per-minute part exists, and every day of the window does. The rows: `agg_trade_id, price, quantity, first_trade_id,
               last_trade_id, transact_time (ms, the exchange's clock), is_buyer_maker` (true: the aggressor SOLD into the bid).
               (2) The raw ladder exports already on the VM, `data/raw/levels/<day>/levels.csv.gz` (one per day, 2026-08-05 → 09-13;
               `symbol, ts, event_time, transaction_time, last_update_id, depth, bids, asks` with bids/asks as JSON arrays of [price, qty],
               best first): the TOUCH — best bid and ask price AND quantity — per snapshot (`data/ladder/<SYM>.parquet` has the prices but
               not the quantities). `ts` is the receipt clock (≈ 160 ms after the exchange's at p50, DATA.md); the snapshot used at a
               placement instant s is the last one with ts ≤ s.
               (3) In hand for the checks: the per-minute tape parts (`data/tape/parts/<SYM>/<day>.parquet`, built from these same files),
               `data/cost_daily.parquet` (P1's `maker_fill_15`, `maker_adv_15`, `spread_cal_bps`, `imp_10000` for the window's days), the
               5m candles (for the harness's bar-level maker on the same placements).
Method:        `ft2/makercost.py` (`ft2 makercost --start 2026-08-15 --end 2026-08-28` → `output/makercost/2026-08-15_2026-08-28/`), per name:
               PLACEMENTS at every 5-minute bar close s of the window (the harness's execution instants; 4,032 a name), both sides each
               time: a BUY resting at the best bid P_b(s) and a SELL at the best ask P_a(s) from the last snapshot at or before s, each of
               10,000 USDT (own quantity q = 10,000 / P). QUEUE: Q0 = the quantity already at that price level in that snapshot (FIFO: the
               order is last at its level; cancellations ahead of it are unobservable and taken as none — the fill share is a LOWER
               bound and the cost an UPPER bound, written as such). FILL: the order fills at the first trade time after s at which either
               (a) the cumulative quantity of trades AT price P on the order's side (for a buy: is_buyer_maker true at price P_b) reaches
               Q0 + q, or (b) a trade prints beyond the level (for a buy: at a price below P_b — the level was swept); a fill within 15
               minutes of s is a fill (the harness's wait: 3 bars), else the order is crossed at s + 15 min. Partial fills (a) with
               cumulative ≥ Q0 but < Q0 + q are counted and reported, not credited. NUMBERS per placement: filled (within 15 min), the time
               to fill, the adverse drift adv = (mid(s + 15 min) − P) / P × 1e4 signed so that negative is bad for the maker (for a sell,
               (P − mid) / P), conditional on the fill — P1's definition at the trade level; for an unfilled order the crossing cost at
               s + 15: the taker fee, the half-spread and the impact at 10,000 USDT from the ladder's `walk` at that instant, and the
               MISSED MOVE (mid(s + 15) − P, signed against the order) reported apart (the harness keeps it in gross). EFFECTIVE ROUND
               TRIP per name = 2 × [ fill × (2.0 − adv_filled) + (1 − fill) × (5.0 + half-spread + impact) ], the missed move excluded (the
               harness's accounting) and included (described). THE HARNESS'S MAKER on the same placements: rest at the 5m CLOSE at s,
               fill if a later bar's low (high) trades strictly through within 3 bars — its fill share and its implied round trip, beside
               P1's day numbers for the window's days (`maker_fill_15`, `maker_adv_15` → `maker_rt_15`).
               Cuts, fixed here: per name; by hour of day (UTC, 24); by the day's realised volatility (the window's days split at the
               median of the name's daily |move|); by the queue ahead at placement in units of own size (Q0 / q: under 1, 1–10, over 10).
Statistic:     per name the effective maker round trip (bps, the missed move excluded) with a day-clustered se over the 14 days (the
               placements of a day are one cluster); the fill share within 15 minutes; the median time to fill; the median Q0 / q. The
               NUMBER the registration asks for: the median over the twelve of the effective round trip, and per name.
Validity:      read first, or the run is void (exit 2): (1) the fetch complete — 12 × 14 files, 0 failed; (2) the trades reproduce the tape:
               per name and day, the sum of `quantity` and the count of trades equal the per-minute parts' `volume` and `n_trades` summed
               over the day to 1e-6 (the parts were built from these files); (3) the ladder present: ≥ 95 % of the placements of every name
               have a snapshot within 60 s before s with a best-level quantity; the raw levels' rows per name-day ≈ 7,000 (reported);
               (4) the clock: trades are stamped by the exchange, snapshots by receipt (≈ 160 ms late at p50, 320–360 at p95, DATA.md) —
               a placement uses the last snapshot with ts ≤ s, so it is at most ~0.4 s stale against the trades, which is inside a 12-s
               cadence; written, not corrected; (5) P1's day numbers for the window's days read from `cost_daily` and shown beside.
Folds read:    none — F5's prices, trades and book over 14 days are read for costs; no rule, no forecast, no label. The guard is not
               involved (`makercost` is not a backtest).
Gate:          not a signal: no CLEARS. The number LICENSES, written before it is read: (a) P2 #7's maker bars re-read (not re-run) with
               the measured round trip per name in the formula `ic_needed = rt / (Z_TOP × 1.2533 × mean|move|)` — one table under this
               block; (b) a `maker_rt_trade` column per name in `cost_daily`'s place for the harness to price from (a change to
               `backtest.price`'s maker is a NEW registration — the harness is not touched by this read); (c) a plain sentence per name:
               the maker path is OPEN if the trade-level round trip is within +1.5 bps of the harness's (P1's) on that name; NARROWER by
               the difference if it is above by 1.5 … 4 bps (every maker verdict in §8 is then re-stated with the measured number as a
               described line — R31's +2, R38's +20, the 4h bars — none re-run); CLOSED for the name if above by more than 4 bps (the
               maker there is a taker who waits). (d) If the twelve's median round trip is ≤ 5 bps, decision O's (O2) logic returns with
               the measured bar — as a new registration, Vadim's. Nothing in money; nothing read on a fold.
Expectation:   written before any number. The touch on BTC and ETH holds millions of USDT (the ±0.2 % band holds tens of millions): a 10,000-
               USDT order last in that queue fills within 15 minutes mostly when the level is SWEPT, not consumed — fill share 50 … 75 %
               (P1's minute rule, which calls a trade-through a fill, read 95–96 %); on the thin names (ZEC, WLD, PEPE, HYPE, AVAX, LINK) the
               touch is small, fills are fast (median under a minute when they come) and the drift after them worse. Adverse drift on fills
               −1 … −3 bps as P1, perhaps −2 … −4 on the majors once only the swept fills count (the fill arrives when the price is
               going through). Effective round trip, the missed move excluded: 7 … 10 bps on the majors (above P1's 6.0 … 6.5), 8 … 11 on
               the thin names (P1's 7 … 9.6); the twelve's median 8 … 9 against the 7.2 the bars use — the harness's maker optimistic by
               about 1 … 2 bps, i.e. "NARROWER", not closed, on most names; CLOSED on none; OPEN on the thin names where the queue is
               short. The missed move on unfilled orders adds 3 … 8 bps more where it is counted. Likeliest sentence: "the maker path is
               narrower than P1 said by 1 … 2 bps on the twelve, and the 4h reversal's and R38's maker verdicts stand as read — sub-cost
               and inside noise — a little further from their bars". The one outcome that would change the record: a median round trip
               ≤ 5 (the queue is shorter than the touch quantity suggests because cancellations are many — unobservable here, so this
               read cannot produce it: its number is an upper bound).
Cost:          a day of code (the fetcher and the ladder parser exist; the FIFO simulation is new), 1 … 2 h of download, 20 min of
               reading; ≈ 5 GB of the VM's 89 GB free.

### R40 — the harness priced from the measured maker: a `maker_trade` execution carrying R39's trade-level numbers per name, and the three maker reads re-executed under it (registered 2026-10-13 on Vadim's "Q1" (P8 decision Q), before the code was written and before any read was made again; read 2026-10-15: validity PASS, no verdict changes, the correction half its written size)
Question:      R39 measured the maker round trip at the trade level on the twelve — 8.43 bps a round trip at the median, 1.7 above the
               harness's bar-level maker on the same placements — and found WHY the bar is kind: it over-fills by 2–4 points (a strict
               trade-through of the bar's close is not a fill of an order at the touch) and understates the drift after the fill by about
               0.5 bps (the fill arrives with the sweep). Every maker number in §8 was priced by that bar-level maker or by P1's day
               average. This registration corrects the INSTRUMENT, not a signal: an execution the harness prices from the measured
               numbers, beside the old ones so that every old number stays reproducible, and the three maker reads made again under it so
               that the record states them at the measured cost. No verdict is expected to change (R39's Result already re-stated them by
               arithmetic: R31 ≈ +0.3, R38 ≈ +18.4); the point is that the harness says it, not the arithmetic.
Execution:     `maker_trade`, a fourth value of `--execs` (`taker`, `maker`, `maker_ev` unchanged, bit for bit — validity (1)). Per name the
               THREE constants R39 measured over 2026-08-15 → 08-28, frozen in `ft2/maker_trade.csv` (committed with this block, from
               `output/makercost/2026-08-15_2026-08-28/summary.csv`): the fill share within 15 minutes p, the mean drift after a fill against
               the resting price adv (negative = bad), and the mean slippage of crossing at 15 minutes slip (bps beyond the fee, the half-
               spread inside) —
                 BTC  0.9255 −1.237 0.010 · ETH 0.9429 −1.357 0.030 · SOL 0.9238 −1.627 0.581 · XRP 0.9317 −2.111 0.535 · ADA 0.8720 −3.206 2.856
                 AVAX 0.9199 −2.208 1.677 · LINK 0.9411 −2.194 1.398 · DOGE 0.9175 −1.796 0.784 · ZEC 0.9626 −2.223 0.846 · PEPE 0.9558 −2.110 1.796
                 WLD  0.9408 −2.372 3.195 · HYPE 0.9543 −2.110 0.623
               A leg is priced at the bar's close with no wait (the EV form of `maker_ev`, path-independent): fee = p × 2.0 + (1 − p) × 5.0,
               other cost = p × (−adv) + (1 − p) × slip, p_fill = p; the exit leg on the position's value as every exec (CHARGED). A round trip
               so priced is R39's `eff_rt` to within 0.012 bps (the mean of the placements' leg costs against the product of the means — the
               largest gap over the twelve, HYPE; written here). A name without a row (any name outside the twelve) gets NaN: unpriced, as a
               name without a cost row is. The constants are ONE fortnight's, applied to every bar of 2020 → 2024: the maker cost is taken as
               its 2026-08 level on every day — P1's daily `maker_adv_15` / `maker_fill_15` series stay what `maker_ev` prices from, and the
               difference between `maker_ev` and `maker_trade` on the same trades IS the measured correction, read as a described row.
Re-executed:   the three maker reads, each by its registered command with `--execs maker_trade` added and `--name <run>_maker_trade`, nothing
               else changed — the decisions and the taker / maker / maker_ev fills identical to the first reads' row by row (validity (2),
               `scripts/actual_check.py trades <first> <re-executed>`, which checks ids, times, prices, fees, costs and funding per exec):
                 R31 `ixhour4h` on FP+F0+F1+F2 (guarded folds, read by R31): `--registration R31 --reexecute maker_trade` — the guard allows
                     a fold read by its registration to be read again once under a tag the plan names (§3's "re-execution `maker_trade`");
                 R38 `ridgebook hold=48 min_bps=10 q_vol=0.9` on F1+F2 (exploration; no guard);
                 R32 `trend1d` on FP+F0+F1+F2: `--registration R32 --reexecute maker_trade` — its maker rows were described, not primary.
               Logged as `R31/maker_trade`, `R32/maker_trade` in `confirmation_reads.csv` beside the first reads, which stay. R17's P7 ledger

### R41 — the funding settlement: does the funding a name is about to pay move its price into the 8-hour settlement and back after, against its peers, on the screener members and on the twelve? (registered 2026-10-15 on Vadim's "R1" (P8 decision R), before the code was written, before the twelve's premium was fetched and before any premium row was read against a 1h or 4h label; read 2026-10-15: VOID before any number of the family — validity (4) FAILED on the members: the median Spearman between fund_due(S − 1 h) and the settled rate 0.776 against the bar 0.8 (88 % within 1 bp; at S itself 0.823 and 92 %); the formula itself right by the label-free diagnostic; decision S for Vadim: R41′ with the formula check at S (recommended) or close)
Question:      Every per-name read so far took a LEVEL or a slow mean (R20: the premium's 1h and 1d means at one day, CLOSED) or an
               unscheduled event (R37). The funding settlement is a SCHEDULED event: every 8 hours (4 on some names and periods) a
               perpetual's longs pay its shorts the funding rate, and the rate is a known function of the premium index averaged over the
               period — F = P + clip(I − P, −5, +5) bps with I = 1 bp per 8 h (0.5 per 4 h), so F sits exactly at I whenever the period's
               mean premium is within [−4, +6] bps (38 % of the settlements in F1+F2 are exactly 0.01 %) and follows P outside. In the
               last hour before the settlement the payment is all but known. The mechanism (the payment-avoidance story): the side that
               pays closes before the settlement and comes back after — the perpetual UNDERPERFORMS its peers into the settlement by an
               amount that grows with the rate due, and RECOVERS after. N1 wrote it as the premium's reversion into and after; the archive's
               5-minute premium index on the 188 members (R20's fetch) and every name's settlement schedule (`funding_archive`, 598 names)
               are in hand; the twelve's premium is one small fetch. The question: on the hour into a settlement and the hours after it,
               does the rate due rank the names' moves against their peers, beyond the plain hourly reversal, and is there money in it?
Cells:         R37's frame. OUTSIDE: `audit.frame` on `output/backtest/r18_transferbook_1d` (the hourly cells of F1+F2, the block's 60
               members, 188 names; the membership mask). THE TWELVE: `audit_index.cells_twelve` on the same grid. The EVENT cells, per
               name: with S each of the name's settlement times (`funding_archive`'s `ts` for the name — the schedule the exchange
               publishes in advance as `next_funding_time`; a convention, written: the realised times are the schedule), INTO = the
               hourly cell t = S − 1 h, AFTER = the cell t = S. The family is NaN on every other cell, so each bar's cross-section is the
               names in an event at that bar (≥ 5, `MIN_PAIRS`; the 4-hour names' extra settlements at 04/12/20 UTC enter where enough of
               them share the hour). A CONTROL cell is any hourly cell that is neither INTO nor AFTER nor within an hour of them.
Labels:        z_h = the log move from the close one bar after t to the close h bars later over σ_1w·√h, clipped at ±5 (`bt.labels`, the
               frame's), at h = 11 for INTO (the close at S − 55 min to the close AT S: the hour into the settlement, nothing after it)
               and h = 12 and 48 for AFTER (S + 5 → S + 65, S + 245). Money in ACTUAL returns against the bar's peers (`horizon.labels`):
               INTO without funding (the position is flat at S and pays nothing), AFTER with funding on value (a 4-hour name's next
               settlement can fall inside the 4 h hold).
Ingredients:   per name and hourly cell t, known strictly before t (a premium bar stamped open_time is used from its close; a settlement
               time is known in advance):
                 P(t)        = the mean premium index (bps) over the period in force, from the last settlement S_prev ≤ t to t, over the
                               bars present (NaN under 60 % of the period's bars); at S − 1 h, 7/8 of what the exchange averages;
                 fund_due(t) = P + clip(I − P, −5, +5), I = 1 bp × interval_h / 8 (the name's interval from its schedule) — the rate due at
                               the next settlement, bps; the per-name caps ignored (rare; written);
                 prem_dev(t) = the last bar's premium − its trailing-30-day mean (N1's form; reference);
                 move_1h(t)  = R37's (the hour's log return in the name's sigmas), for the plain reversal.
Family:        signed so that a POSITIVE IC is the hypothesis: f_into = −fund_due on the INTO cells at h 11; f_after = +fund_due on the
               AFTER cells at h 12 and h 48. Three numbers × two universes = SIX. Nothing fitted, no threshold.
Reference:     described, no verdict, the same cells and shifts: P in the same three slots (if it reads as fund_due the clamp matters
               nothing; if P reads and fund_due does not, the mechanism is the premium's reversion, not the payment); prem_dev the same;
               funding_last (the previous settled rate, R20's feature) the same; rev_1h = −move_1h on the same cells (the plain reversal,
               R37's known fact), and for every family number the paired Δ against rev_1h under the same shifts (u_Δ): whether the rate
               due ADDS to the plain reversal — on the AFTER cells especially, since a dip into S and a snap after IS a reversal; the
               run's forecast (R18's ridge) on the event cells.
Control:       described, decides a verdict's WORDING: the same six numbers on the CONTROL cells (−fund_due at h 11 and +fund_due at h 12,
               48 on hourly cells away from any settlement), under the same shifts. A family number that clears while its control clears
               with |IC_c| at least half its own is "NOT THE SETTLEMENT'S": the premium predicts the next hour everywhere, which is R20's
               premium at a shorter horizon, not the event — recorded, nothing licensed.
Money:         described, actual returns against the bar's peers, before trading costs, with the HAC se over days and the shift null
               (centre, se, u). On each event bar with ≥ 10 names in the event: the FIFTHS — INTO: short the top fifth of fund_due across
               the names in the event, long the bottom fifth (S − 55 → S, no funding); AFTER: long the top fifth, short the bottom fifth
               (S + 5 → S + 65 and → S + 245, funding on value). The mean bps a position earns, per universe and slot; the count of event
               bars and positions; by the interval (8 h / 4 h names) and by the settlement hour (00 / 08 / 16 UTC) described. Against the
               cost: the members' TAKER round trip 18 bps (R20 D3), the twelve's 12.3 — a maker fill at a fixed-time event everyone sees is
               not R39's unconditioned fill and is not assumed. The PROFILE: the mean actual return against the peers per 5-minute bar from
               S − 60 to S + 60 min, signed by the INTO position's side (−sign(fund_due)), on the fifths — where in the two hours the
               move sits; described.
Statistic:     R37's: per bar the Spearman across the names present (≥ 5 with feature and label), averaged per day; IC = the mean over
               days; the HAC t over days beside, deciding nothing.
Null:          R37's: the labels move by a whole number of days, the same for every name and bar (time of day kept — the settlement hours
               stay settlement hours under the null, which is the point), every admissible shift with gap = 1 (the period, 8 h → a day)
               + 1 (the longest hold, 4 h → a day) + 1 = 3 days: 485 days → 480 shifts, the same shift on both universes, every slot and
               the control; centre, se, IC_c = IC − centre, u = IC_c / se; per shift the largest |u| of the SIX → the family-wise p.
Validity:      read first, or the run is void (exit 2): (1) the frame's — OUTSIDE `audit.frame`'s (the 288-bar labels equal R18's on every
               cell to 1e-6), THE TWELVE `cells_twelve`'s against R14's run; (2) whole days of 24 bars, 485 − 2·3 + 1 = 480 shifts;
               (3) the premium and the schedule read nothing at or after their bar (a test on made-up rows before the real ones: a premium
               changed from a cut on changes no ingredient at or before the cut); fund_due present on ≥ 95 % of the members' event cells
               and ≥ 90 % of the twelve's, else FAIL; (4) the FORMULA: at every settlement S with ≥ 10 names, the Spearman across names
               between fund_due(S − 1 h) and the archive's settled rate at S — its median over the settlements ≥ 0.8 and the share of
               (name, S) within 1 bp of the settled rate ≥ 0.5, else the rate due is not what was written and the run is void; (5) the
               twelve's premium: `premium.parquet` is rewritten whole by the ingest, so the members' rows must come back identical — per
               symbol the row count and the sum of the premium before and after (`scripts/r41_premium_check.py`), FAIL → void.
Folds read:    F1+F2 (exploration) on both universes; cells read before for other features, for the premium at these cells and horizons a
               new question. No confirmation fold; the guard is not involved. The twelve's premium: 11 names (HYPE has no bar in F1+F2).
                 `vm.sh bgsh r41 'bash scripts/r41_chain.sh'`: the fetch (`archive premiumIndexKlines/5m --symbols <the eleven> --monthly
                 --start 2023-04-01 --end 2024-08-31`), the members' fingerprint, the ingest of the 199 names, the fingerprint again and the
                 compare, then `audit r18_transferbook_1d --family settle --twelve --jobs 4` → output/audit/r18_transferbook_1d_settle/;
                 the chain powers the VM off 30 minutes after its last marker unless stopped first (the R40 lesson).
Gate:          validity PASS, then per family number (slot × universe): CLEARS if |u| ≥ 2 AND family-wise p ≤ 0.05 AND the IC has one sign
               in F1 and in F2 AND IC_c > 0 (the registered sign) AND u_Δ ≥ 2 against rev_1h on the same cells and shifts (ADDS to the plain
               reversal) AND the control does not clear at half its size (else "NOT THE SETTLEMENT'S"). "CLEARS AS THE PLAIN REVERSAL"
               without the u_Δ condition; "CLEARS WITH THE OPPOSITE SIGN" with IC_c < 0 (the payers' side RIDES the move: N1's reversion
               read the other way — recorded, nothing licensed); CLOSED if |IC_c| + 1.96 se < 0.02; NOT DETECTABLE otherwise, with its
               MDE (2.8 se). A CLEARS proper on either universe licenses ONE registration, R42: the smallest priced rule that trades the
               event — the fifths of the Money paragraph as its trigger, fixed here, not searched — as a TAKER on the clearing universe
               at the clearing slot, through the harness on F1+F2 with its own gate and the money rows as its expectation; only if that
               rule clears, a confirmation on F3+F4 (the members' F3+F4 premium would be a fetch). Nothing in money here. None clears →
               the settlement is PARKED as "not shown on these cells"; the money rows and the profile stay a described fact.
Power:         written before any number. The members: ≈ 3 event bars a day in each slot (the 8-hour names; the 4-hour names add bars
               with fewer names), ≈ 60 names a bar: a bar's Spearman has se ≈ 0.13, a day's mean of three ≈ 0.075, over 485 days
               ≈ 0.0035 → MDE ≈ 0.010; the ties in fund_due (the dead band holds about 60 % of the names at a bar) cost some of that.
               The twelve: ≈ 11 names a bar, se ≈ 0.32 a bar, 0.18 a day, 0.008 over the days → MDE ≈ 0.023 — only a large effect is
               readable there. The money bar: at 1h the members' round trip of 18 bps against a mean |1h move against the peers| of
               ≈ 60 bps asks IC ≈ 0.14 on all names; the fifths concentrate it, and the money rows say what the fifths earn.
Expectation:   the members, INTO at h 11: fund_due IC_c +0.01 … +0.03, u 2–5, likelier than not (the avoidance is mechanical where the
               rate is large — 24 % of the settlements pay more than 1 bp), ADDS to rev_1h (the plain reversal on the INTO cell is the
               reversal of the hour BEFORE, a different thing) one time in two; AFTER at h 12: +0.00 … +0.02, and ADDING to the plain
               reversal the hard part (the snap IS a reversal of the dip): u_Δ ≥ 2 one time in four; AFTER at h 48: nothing (±0.01). P
               reads like fund_due or a little weaker; prem_dev weaker; funding_last weaker than fund_due (the previous period, not this
               one). The control near zero (if it is not, R20's premium-at-1h, CLOSED, comes back at an hour and the verdict says so).
               The twelve: inside noise on every slot. Money: the fifths INTO +3 … +8 bps a position against the peers on the members
               (under the 18 bps round trip), AFTER at 1h +2 … +6, at 4h ±5; the profile's move in the last 15–30 minutes before S and
               the first 15 after. Likeliest verdict on the six: CLEARS or CLEARS AS THE PLAIN REVERSAL on the members' INTO row, NOT
               DETECTABLE elsewhere; a CLEARS proper that licenses R42 one time in three; the money under its cost bar everywhere, so R42,
               if licensed, is a hypothesis about a mechanism priced as a taker, not a trade found. Half a day: the registration, the
               code and its tests (a planted dip-and-snap on made-up bars with a made-up schedule comes back with the registered signs,
               ADDS, and the control is flat; a world without the premium voids the run; the formula check), the fetch (minutes), the run
               (≈ 30–60 min: six family numbers, the references and the control under 480 shifts), the read.

               the shifts; M_c = M − centre; u = M_c / se; the family 2 × 2 = 4: per shift the largest |u| of the four → the family-wise p.

### R50 — BTC's last hour as per-name information: does a name that lagged BTC's hour catch up against its peers over the next 1h / 4h / 1d, and does BTC's hour carry on through the high-beta names? Stage 1 on F1+F2 (the members and the twelve), stage 2 on F3+F4 for the cells that clear, once (registered 2026-10-18 on Vadim's "AD1" (P8 decision AD), before any code was written and before any crypto bar was read against BTC's hour; stage 1 read 2026-10-18: VALIDITY PASS and **0 of 12 CLEAR — lead_1h CLEARS AS THE PLAIN REVERSAL at 1h and 4h on both universes and at 1d on the members (IC_c +0.018 / +0.017 / +0.005 on the members, +0.025 / +0.022 on the twelve; u 3–11, family-wise p 0.0024–0.033) and ADDS NOTHING to the plain reversal (Δ against rev_1h −0.0015 … +0.0007, u_Δ −3.2 … +1.4 — at 1h on the members BTC's term SUBTRACTS); bx_1h CLOSED at every horizon on both universes (IC_c −0.007 … +0.001, every upper bound under 0.02); the twelve's lead at 1d CLOSED. Described: the high-beta names give back after a BTC FALL (bx −0.016 / −0.023 / −0.032 at 1h / 4h / 1d on the members, t −5 / −5 / −2.9) and not after a rise (+0.000 / +0.002 / +0.011) — a sign asymmetry inside a closed family, a line for a successor, not a finding**; stage 2 NOT RUN — NOTHING TO CONFIRM, F3+F4 unread for this family)
Question:      Decision AA's AA4 (Y6 / U4), decision AD's AD1. R26 read the US index as per-name information through each name's beta and found
               nothing (the index's move is in crypto within minutes). BTC is the crypto market's own index, traded round the clock on the same
               venue, and every alt is quoted against it by every desk: when BTC moves in an hour, the alts move with it — but not all at once
               and not all by their beta. Two questions on the hour just closed, per name and against its peers: (a) CATCH-UP — a name that
               moved LESS than its beta to BTC said it should have (it lagged) moves toward BTC's lead over the next hours; (b) CARRY-ON — BTC's
               hour continues through the high-beta names (or reverses in them, R26's "beta after an index rise" lesson). The plain
               cross-sectional hourly reversal (R37: a name's own last hour reversed, IC +0.02 … +0.03 at 1h, u 7–11, far under its cost) is the
               known fact that (a) contains and must BEAT: a catch-up row that does not add to the plain reversal is the plain reversal again.
Cells:         STAGE 1, exploration — R26's / R37's frame exactly. OUTSIDE: R18's cells (`audit.frame` on `output/backtest/r18_transferbook_1d`:
               the hourly decision bars of F1+F2, embargoed, the block's 60 members, the twelve left out; 694,501 cells, 188 names, 485 days) as the
               membership mask; the labels at 12, 48 and 288 bars where they exist. THE TWELVE: `audit_index.cells_twelve` on the same grid
               (125,462 cells, 11 names; checked against R14's decisions as R26 did); BTC's own cells are NOT cells here (its beta is 1 and its
               lag 0 by definition — NaN, as R27's beta_btc), so 10 names a bar. The same grid, the same shifts for both universes.
               STAGE 2, confirmation, once and only for the cells that clear stage 1: the F3+F4 MEMBERS — `ft2/screen_members_f34.csv` (216
               names, the 60 most-traded outside the twelve in each 30-day block; R44's universe) on the hourly grid of F3+F4, embargoed, a cell
               where the name is a member of the block containing t and has a close at t, a σ_1w and the label; the twelve on F3+F4 by
               `cells_twelve(folds F3 F4)` checked against `r16_ridgebook_1d_ho12_f34`'s forecast. The klines, funding and costs of both are in
               hand (R25, R29, R44). If NO cell clears stage 1, stage 2 is not run and F3+F4 stays unread for this family.
Labels:        z_h = the log move from the close one bar after t to the close h bars later over σ_1w·√h, clipped at ±5 (`horizon.run`'s Zh; the
               frame R20–R37 used), at h = 12 (1h), 48 (4h), 288 (1d).
Ingredients:   per name and hourly bar t, known strictly before t (the candles closed at t; nothing of BTC's or the name's bar after t):
                 r_1h       = the name's log return over the last 12 bars, bps; b_1h = BTC's (BTCUSDT's 5m close from the same market; the
                              SAME number on both universes at every bar — a validity line)
                 beta_btc   = the least-squares slope of the name's hourly log return on BTC's over the 720 hours before t (≥ 200 finite pairs,
                              else NaN; R27's `_beta`; every hour counts — BTC never closes)
                 σ_1h       = σ_1w·√12, the name's trailing-week 5m sd scaled to the hour (`_derive`'s sig 1w)
Family:        two features, in the name's own hourly sigmas (the statistic ranks across names; the unit fixes which names are compared on
               what):
                 lead_1h = (beta_btc × b_1h − r_1h) / σ_1h     what BTC's hour said the name should have moved minus what it did: POSITIVE when
                                                              the name lagged a rise or out-fell a fall; the CATCH-UP hypothesis is a POSITIVE IC
                 bx_1h   = beta_btc × b_1h / σ_1h              BTC's hour through the name's beta; two-sided (carry-on +, over-reaction −)
               × three horizons (12, 48, 288) × two universes = 12 numbers. Nothing fitted, no threshold.
Reference:     described, no verdict, the same frame and shifts: rev_1h = −r_1h / σ_1h (R37's plain reversal, the fact lead_1h must beat);
               beta_btc alone (a level); and per lead_1h cell the PAIRED difference against rev_1h on the same cells under the same shifts,
               Δ = IC_c(lead_1h) − IC_c(rev_1h), u_Δ from the shifts' sd of the difference — whether BTC's term ADDS to the plain reversal.
               Described beside: lead_1h and bx_1h split by the sign of b_1h (after a BTC rise / fall); lead_1h by S90 (R45's state at the

### R51 — token unlocks on the members: what a name does against its peers over the week INTO a promised cliff and over the 1, 3 and 7 days AFTER it. Stage 1 on F1+F2's promised events, stage 2 on F3+F4's for the rows that clear, once (registered 2026-10-18 on Vadim's "Ok AE1" (P8 decision AE), before any code was written and before any bar was read against an unlock; stage 1 read 2026-10-18: VALIDITY PASS on every line and **0 of 4 CLEAR — every row NOT DETECTABLE: the week INTO a promised cliff −216 bps against the peers (se 114, u −1.9, family-wise p 0.18, MDE 319; the sign the record predicted, 74 % of the 86 events below zero, median −367, both folds negative), the 1 / 3 / 7 days AFTER +22 / −1 / −76 (u 0.5 / 0.0 / −0.7). Question:      Decision AA's AA3 (Y4 / §9 #8), decision AE's AE1. A token unlock is a block of a token held back for the team, investors or a
               treasury that becomes sellable on a published date — known weeks ahead, per name, and about exactly the young names the
               screener holds. The one hypothesis in the record whose mechanism is a KNOWN supply shock on a KNOWN date, which no
               cross-sectional read can see. Two questions, no direction fixed (R28's rule: nothing measured here has chosen one): (a) INTO —
               does the name move against its peers over the week before the cliff (holders selling ahead of the supply, or buying the dip
               others sell); (b) AFTER — over the 1, 3 and 7 days after it (the released tokens sold, or the overhang lifted). The source
               audit of 2026-10-05 (DATA.md `unlock_asof`) fixed the known-at rule this read obeys to the letter: an unlock is used as the
               LAST archived page at least 7 days before it dated it (`events.promised`), never from today's file, which is re-drawn as it
               ages (38–46 % of what a 2023–25 page dated is not in today's file as dated).
Events:        the point-in-time table, frozen BEFORE any price is read: `events.promised` on the cliff days of the 81 Wayback snapshots of
               defillama.com/unlocks (`data/unlock_asof.parquet`, aligned to today's ids; a protocol's cliffs on one UTC day one event; size ≥
               0.1 % of the maximum supply — the inventory's dust line), joined by ticker to the members WHILE THEY ARE MEMBERS (the 30 days of
               the block holding the day; `events.in_blocks`): stage 1 the F1+F2 members (`ft2/screen_members.csv`), stage 2 the F3+F4
               members (`ft2/screen_members_f34.csv`). One event per (perpetual, day). Written by `scripts/r51_unlocks.py select` on the work

               today's schedule) and committed before the first bar is loaded for this read. Expected from the inventory: 36 + 54 = 90 events
               on F1+F2 (22 names, the ten with the most holding nine in ten), 58 + 20 = 78 on F3+F4 (F4's 20 are the ones the 30-day pages
               reach); F5's 5 are too few for anything and are not read. A 2026-10-05 fingerprint of the two parquet files (rows, md5) is
               written into validity. The twelve are not read (seven have a schedule; the twelve are not members and were walked by R14 over
               these days — a different question, not this one).
Entry:         per event the cliff day D (UTC midnight, the day the page dated). AFTER: the decision bar is the one closing at D 00:00 UTC,

Label:         per event and row, bps of the position's size at entry, R28's `listing.label_at` (= `horizon.labels`' second number: exit ÷

Family:        four rows, two-sided: into_7d, after_1d, after_3d, after_7d; M_r = the mean of y over the events. Nothing fitted, no threshold.
Null:          every admissible WHOLE-DAY shift of the event dates, the same k for every event (R26's / R50's form: the calendar structure of

### R54 — magnitude against implied: does P2's realised-volatility forecast add to Deribit's implied volatility index in forecasting BTC's and ETH's realised volatility over the next 1 and 7 days? (registered 2026-10-18 on Vadim's "AK2" (P8 decision AK), before any DVOL value was fetched and before any code was written; read 2026-10-18: VALIDITY PASS, 2 of 4 ALIVE — the candles add to the implied at ONE day (BTC ΔR² +0.11, t 3.7; ETH +0.07, t 2.4; both folds) and not at a week (BTC −0.04 NOT DETECTABLE, ETH −0.09 CLOSED, where the implied beyond the candles reads +0.11 / +0.16); the frame OPEN by the gate at the one-day horizon, the week the implied's; decision AL written)
Question:      P2 #1 is the one finding of this project with power: how much a price will move is predictable out of sample (R² 16 % at
               15m, 11 % at 4h, 5 % at 1d) while which way is not. Within the perpetuals' frame that is only a multiplier. The product that
               pays for a magnitude forecast is variance — options, or Deribit's DVOL futures — on the three names Deribit lists (BTC, ETH,
               SOL). Before any paid data, one audit on free data decides whether the line is alive at all: the market already publishes
               its own magnitude forecast, Deribit's implied volatility index (DVOL, the 30-day implied vol in annualised %, daily since
               2021-03-24 for BTC). Does the candle-built realised-vol forecast carry anything BEYOND it about the realised volatility of
               the next day and the next week? If it does not, the frame closes without buying a single option quote; if it does, the next
               question is the variance product's cost, not its signal.
Data:          (1) DVOL — `ft2 dvol fetch|ingest|inventory` (`ft2/dvol.py`): Deribit's public, keyless JSON-RPC endpoint
               `public/get_volatility_index_data` (currency, start/end ms, resolution 1D → candles [ts, open, high, low, close], 100 a call,
               paginated by `continuation`), for BTC, ETH and SOL from 2021-01-01 to the fetch day; raw under `data/raw/external/deribit/
               dvol_<CUR>_1D_<YYYYMMDD>.json` (a dated copy per fetch), ingested to `data/dvol.parquet`: `(currency, day) → open, high, low,
               close`; the inventory writes the extent per currency, the gaps, the range, and a DATA.md row before the audit reads it. The
               VALUE KNOWN AT 00:00 UTC of day d is the OPEN of day d's candle (Deribit's day is UTC; the row's ts 00:00); the audit reads
               `open` and nothing else of the row. (2) The 5-minute candles of BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT (the collector's, with the archive's
               klines under them from 2019-12-31 — `ceiling.panel(..., start=2021-01-01)`), for the target and the candle features. Nothing
               else; no option quote, no fee table.
Target:        y_h(d) = log RV_h(d), the realised volatility of the h days from 00:00 of day d: RV = √(365/h × Σ r²) × 100 in annualised %,
               r the 5-minute log returns of the close over [d, d + h), h ∈ {1, 7}; a day with fewer than 95 % of its 288 bars is not a
               target day and not inside another's window (dropped and counted).
Features:      at 00:00 of day d, from bars strictly before d: the candle set C = { log RV_1 (day d − 1), log RV_7 (d − 7 … d − 1),
               log RV_30 (d − 30 … d − 1), dvs = log(dollar volume of d − 1 / its mean over d − 30 … d − 1) } — the HAR ladder of
               realised volatility plus P2's dollar-volume surprise (P2 #3: the two inputs that carry IC ≈ 0.2 for |move|); the implied
               set I = { log DVOL_open(d) }. Fixed here; no other feature, lag or transform.
Models:        per name and horizon, three ordinary least-squares fits WITH an intercept (a level is the right prior for volatility):
               I alone, C alone, I + C — refitted every 30 days on every row whose target window ended before the block's first day
               (the harness's rule, R7), the rows accruing from 2021-03-24 (DVOL's first day; the pre-history and F0 are training rows,
               never scored); scored on F1+F2's whole days. Out-of-sample R² on the scored days = 1 − Σ(y − ŷ)² / Σ(y − ȳ_scored)²; the
               per-day squared-error loss of each model.
Statistic:     per name × horizon the LOSS DIFFERENCE L_I − L_{I+C} per scored day (positive: the candles improve on the implied), its mean
               with a Newey–West se over days (lags h + 1), t = mean / se; ΔR² = that mean / the scored days' mean total variance (the
               same number in R² units); per fold beside. The reverse, L_C − L_{I+C} (what the implied adds to the candles), described
               with the same statistic, no verdict. Also described: each model's R² per fold; the I + C coefficients at the last refit;
               the variance risk premium as context — the mean of log DVOL_open(d) − log RV_30(d) over the scored days; SOL's rows if its
               DVOL covers F1+F2 (outside the family, no verdict).
Family:        FOUR rows — BTC and ETH × 1 and 7 days — of "the candles beyond the implied"; the one-sided bar for four at 5 %: t ≥ 2.24.
Validity:      read first, or the run is void and the cause found before any number: (1) DVOL present on ≥ 99 % of the scored days of each
               name, every value in [10, 300], no duplicate day, the row's ts at 00:00 UTC; the feature is the OPEN (a test plants a
               post-midnight value in `close` and shows the forecast unchanged); (2) the scored days whole (dropped days counted and ≤ 2 %
               of F1+F2); (3) causal: the features at d recomputed on the panel cut at d identical, and a planted series in the tests;
               (4) every refit's rows have target windows ended before the block's first day; (5) the folds by `folds.bounds` with the
               embargo; (6) the target recomputed from the candles in the test equals the formula to 1e-9.
Folds read:    F1+F2 (exploration) on BTC and ETH; FP and F0 as training rows only; nothing from F3–F5; no backtest, no guard.
Gate:          per family row: THE LINE IS ALIVE on that row if t ≥ 2.24 AND ΔR² ≥ 0.02 AND the loss difference is positive in F1 and in
               F2; CLOSED if ΔR² + 1.96 × (se / mean total variance) < 0.02; else NOT DETECTABLE with its MDE (2.8 se). Any row alive →
               the frame is OPEN and the next registration is the variance product's COST (Deribit's fee schedule, the option spread, a
               delta-hedged straddle's realised PnL from the forecast's sign against the implied), which needs option prices the project
               does not hold — a source audit first (Deribit's public trade history, Tardis), and the budget Vadim's call. No row alive →
               the magnitude frame is CLOSED for a product; P2 #1's multiplier stays what it is. No variant on these days under this
               registration: no other feature, horizon, learner, name, or fit window; a 30-day horizon is NOT read (sixteen months hold
               16 non-overlapping months — no power).
Expectation:   written before any value is fetched. At 1 day: R² of I alone 0.35 … 0.55, C alone 0.45 … 0.65 (the HAR ladder beats the
               30-day implied at a day in the literature), ΔR² of C beyond I +0.05 … +0.20 with t 3 … 6 on both names — ALIVE the
               likeliest at 1d; the reverse +0.00 … +0.03. At 7 days the implied catches up: ΔR² 0 … +0.08, t 0 … 3 — NOT DETECTABLE or
               ALIVE; the reverse larger than at 1d. The variance risk premium positive, +0.1 … +0.3 in log units (the implied above the
               realised on average). Validity PASS, under 1 % of days dropped. The named likeliest verdict: 2 of 4 alive (the 1d rows),
               the 7d rows not detectable — the frame OPEN, with the honest note written now that a one-day volatility edge is the harder
               one to monetise through options (the tenor and the daily gamma costs), so the 7d rows are the ones a product would need.
