               ≈ 0.05 … 0.08 there, so a small 7d gain is not detectable on F1+F2 and is not refuted by "not detectable".
Commands:      on the work VM — `ft2 dvol fetch && ft2 dvol ingest && ft2 dvol inventory` (minutes; the DATA.md row written from the
               inventory before the audit), then `ft2 magvol --holds 1 7` → output/magvol/f12/magvol.md, rows.csv, loss.csv, coef.csv,

Result:        **Read 2026-10-18 (the block registered in 2b3a843 before any fetch or code, the code d739a9f; the chain on the work VM

### R55 — varbook: the one-day variance position on BTC and ETH, signed by R54's forecast against the straddle's own implied, at Deribit's prices and the project's hedge costs — does it pay? (registered 2026-10-18 on Vadim's "AL1" after the source audit, before any series value was fetched — the audit's 20 probe days a name are the only option prices in hand; read 2026-10-19)
Question:      R54 says the candles know a tenth of tomorrow's log realised variance beyond the 30-day implied, on both names. The one
               product with that tenor is a one-day variance position: the at-the-money straddle expiring the next day, bought when the
               forecast says the day will move more than the straddle prices, sold when less, delta-hedged through the day, settled at
               expiry. Its costs are known to be large for the tenor — the spread at the touch, four fee events, the hedge's crossings.
               Does the forecast's sign pay them on F1+F2's days, at Deribit's own prices? If the gross pays and the net does not, the
               verdict is R39's "REAL, NOT FUNDED" and the line's next question is the venue (Binance's tighter touch, a maker entry); if
               neither pays, the magnitude frame closes for a product.
Data:          (1) `ft2 straddle fetch|ingest|inventory` (new, `ft2/straddle.py`): for each day d of F1+F2 (2023-05-01 → 2024-08-31) and
               each name (BTC, ETH), from Deribit's public chart endpoint (DATA.md `deribit_options`): the perpetual's 1-minute open at
               00:00 of d (the spot S), the at-the-money strike K on the exchange's grid nearest S, the daily-expiry call and put
               `<CUR>-<d+1>-<K>-C/P` (expiring 08:00 UTC of d + 1) as hourly bars over [d − 1 00:00, d + 1 08:00] (the strikes tried
               nearest first until both legs are served; a day with no served pair is skipped and counted), and the perpetual's 1-minute
               bars 07:30 → 08:00 of d + 1 (the settlement window: Deribit delivers at the 30-minute TWAP of the index before 08:00 —
               the perpetual's TWAP stands in, the approximation stated) and its hourly closes over the day (the hedge's prices). Raw
               under `data/raw/external/deribit/straddle/<CUR>/<day>.json`, ingested to `data/straddle_1d.parquet`; the inventory writes
               the coverage per fold and a DATA.md table before the read. (2) `ft2 straddle quotes`: Tardis's free-day `quotes` files
               for the SAME two legs on each first-of-month day of F1+F2 (16 days × 2 names × 2 legs, ≈ 0.3 MB each; per-instrument files
               only — DATA.md `tardis`), raw under `data/raw/external/tardis/quotes/`: the bid and ask at the first update at or after
               00:00 and the median spread over hour 0, in bps of spot. (3) R54's per-day forecasts as written: `output/magvol/f12/
               loss.csv`, column `yhat_I+C` at hold 1 (the file's sha256 recorded in validity; no refit, no other column). (4) The
               project's taker cost for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT for the hedge: `makercost.TAKER_BPS` (5) + half the calibrated spread of the
               day (`cost_daily`) — Binance's numbers, measured here; Deribit's perpetual (3.5 bps taker) stated beside, not used.
Entry:         at 00:00 of d, each leg at its LAST TRADED price before 00:00 (the last bar with volume > 0 in [d − 1 00:00, d 00:00)); a
               leg with no trade in those 24 hours, or a pair failing put–call parity (|C − P − (S − K)/S| > 0.5 % of spot, prices in
               units of spot) is stale: the day is skipped and counted. The straddle's mid m = C + P (in units of spot). The crossing
               cost: half the touch spread per leg, taken as ONE constant per name — the median over the 16 free days of the at-the-money
               straddle's spread at 00:00 in bps of spot (its range reported) — paid at entry; the exit is the settlement (no exit
               crossing). Fees: 0.03 % of spot a leg at entry (under the 12.5 %-of-premium cap on a 2 % straddle), 0.015 % a leg at
               delivery (the unconfirmed third-party figure, taken as written — conservative); the hedge's crossings at (4).
Sign:          the straddle's break-even volatility σ_q = m / (0.8 × √(32 / 8760)) (the at-the-money approximation; annualised, in the
               units of R54's target); the forecast RV̂ = exp(ŷ_{I+C}(d)) / 100 (R54's log-vol forecast in annualised units). LONG
               variance (buy the straddle) if log RV̂ > log σ_q, SHORT if below; no threshold, no sizing: one straddle per unit of spot,
               every covered day. R54's forecast is of the 24 hours from 00:00; the straddle covers 32 — stated, not adjusted.
Hedge:         Black–Scholes delta of the straddle at σ_q and the hours to 08:00 of d + 1, recomputed at each hourly close of the
               perpetual from 00:00 of d to 07:00 of d + 1 (32 hedges), the hedge trade = the change in delta × spot, each paid the taker
               cost of (4); the hedge's PnL = Σ (position held over the hour × the hour's price change). The unhedged position (no hedge
               trades) described beside.
PnL:           per covered day, in bps of spot per straddle: sign × [ |S_T − K| − m + hedge PnL ] − crossing − fees − hedge crossings,
               S_T the settlement TWAP. Gross = the bracket × sign (before every cost).
Statistic:     per name the mean net PnL per covered day, Newey–West se (lags 2), t; per fold; the gross with the same statistic; the cost
               decomposition (crossing, option fees, hedge crossings) as means; the hit rate of the sign on the realised against σ_q; the
               always-SHORT and always-LONG rows (the variance premium in money, and its opposite) described; the unhedged rows described;
               R54's I-alone and C-alone forecasts as the sign — described, no verdict (the family is I + C).
Family:        TWO rows — BTC and ETH, hedged, signed by R54's I + C forecast; the one-sided bar for two at 5 %: t ≥ 1.96.
Validity:      read first, or the run is void and the cause found: (1) causal entry — every bar read for an entry ends at or before 00:00 of

Folds read:    F1+F2 (exploration), on R54's own scored days; nothing from F3–F5; no backtest harness (the book is priced here).

Expectation:   written before any series value is fetched. Costs: the touch 10 … 15 % of the straddle's mid (2023-06-01 10 %, today 12 %) =

### R56 — magvolq: R54's forecast against the ONE-DAY implied — does the candle-and-index forecast add to the straddle's own break-even volatility in forecasting BTC's and ETH's realised volatility over the next day?                cells, under its cost bar) at a slower clock, where one round trip is paid against a week's dispersion.

               the liquid names (a day's autocorrelation 0.8 on BTC / ETH), per name more than market-wide (the first component 25 %).

               when a name trades richer on Coinbase than it has over its own trailing month (US spot demand on that name), or richer
               than a day ago, does it then do worse or better than the other names over the next day? A ceiling screen in P2's frame,
               not a rule: it spends no fold and licenses, at most, the smallest rule that trades it on F1+F2.

               (`ceiling.panel` on the twelve, `derive`, F1+F2 embargoed as the scored sample, `ic_screen`'s three statistics on every
               P2 horizon; the relative cross-sectional Spearman is the bet of this question), on three bar × name features from ONE
               source, `data/coinbase_1h.parquet`'s adjusted premium (bps), read at the last hourly bar whose `ts_known` + 5 min ≤ t
               (the bar's start + 1 h, plus one 5m bar of margin for the serving lag — fixed here whatever the lag measured says):
                 cbprem          the level at t — DESCRIBED, not gated (a series this slow is flattered by a day-shuffle null; its

                 cbprem_chg_1d   = (cbprem − cbprem 24 hourly bars earlier) / the same sd — the second registered feature.

               (sd ≈ 48 bps) and PEPE / WLD / HYPE have no F1+F2 bars — their columns are NaN in the registered frames; a DESCRIBED row
               repeats the two features with ZEC's column in (no nulls). The family: the two registered features × the two horizons

### R61 — the money shape of R60's found sign on F1+F2: when the names are ranked by how far their Coinbase premium sits above their own month, is the next day's spread between the top and the bottom name linear in rank and small, or carried by the extremes?                times the linear spread. The screen averages every bar and cannot say; this description says, in bps, on the same cells.
               Seen cells and a sign chosen after R60's look: numbers to size a rule by, NOT a test. Written as such.

               scored bars, the 8 liquid names, the hourly bar read from ts_known + 5 min on): the label is the name's 1d forward
               return in bps (`D["fwd"]["1d"]`, P2's) minus the mean over the liquid names present at t (≥ 5) — "relative". Tables:

Rule for adding any of them: a raw download lands under `data/raw/external/<source>/`, is
ingested by `ft2 ingest` into its own parquet, and gets a row in DATA.md with its measured
extent and its integrity check before any phase reads it.
